text:
Ari: heads-up — p99 spike at stl-pop starting ~10:13 UTC, short request latency tripled. cc @Ben @Priya
Ben: confirmed — p50 stable but p95 jumped 60->180ms and p99 ~420ms, throughput down ~15%. linked flamegraph: https://redwood.dev/flame/1923456789 :thinking_face:
Priya: any prod deploys or config changes?
Ari: no deploys. net-eng alerted to increased hop counts to our STL edge toward transit provider G, and intermittent packet reordering on some flows.
ops-bot: deploy-check: no rolling deploys detected; autoscaler unchanged.
Sam: pulled perf profiles from affected hosts — kernel-selector logs show rapid switches between kernels `fast-attn-v2` and `compat-v1` when RTT spikes; every switch collapses batching and increases per-token latency.
Sam: logs excerpt:
```
kernel-selector: epoch=171; chosen=compat-v1; fallback_reason=packet_reorder; batch_latency_ms=23->140
kernel-selector: epoch=172; chosen=fast-attn-v2; batch_miss=12; kvcache_miss=8
```
Priya: KV cache hit-rate on stl-pop dropped from ~92% to ~65% during the window — looks like requests are being redistributed across hosts which cold-starts KV caches.
Ben: traceroute from one of the clients shows path flapping through peer ASN 64512 -> 65555 -> transit Z, adding 30-40ms intermittently. could be BGP churn or ECMP imbalance. @Jordan any visibility?
Jordan: net-eng: saw IS-IS and BGP adj refreshes with provider Z between 10:12-10:20; provider reported a flapped interface and rerouted some prefixes. opened ticket with them and applied a prepull on our side for affected prefixes. still seeing packet reordering on ~10% of flows.
Ari: short mitigation applied: pinned kernel-selector to `fast-attn-v2` on the impacted rack and temporarily increased batching timeout from 8ms -> 20ms to tolerate the added jitter without thrashing kernels. toggled on at 10:25 UTC.
Sam: after pin + timeout bump p99 dropped to ~160ms within 6 minutes and throughput recovered. will keep pin in place until provider confirms stable routing and we have a longer-term selector fix.
Priya: I'll open a perf/regression ticket and add a canary that simulates transient RTT spikes to prevent selector from being too reactive. INF-2897 created with logs, flamegraphs, and KV cache metrics.
Ari: thanks everyone — follow-ups: (1) net-eng continue provider escalation, (2) infra/serving tune kernel-selector hysteresis and add route-awareness, (3) devex add a small test in CI to simulate peering jitter.
Ben: noted. thanks — :thumbsup:
Ari: tagging #eng-runtime for visibility.
